clues: Water arriving through the air sustains organisms in a place where flowing water is often temporary.
Its sand has travelled through a linked system of rivers, ocean currents and wind.
An older partly consolidated dune system lies beneath a younger, active system.
Fog is a major water source for the invertebrates, reptiles and mammals adapted to this coastal desert.
On Namibia’s Atlantic coast, find the vast fog-influenced dune landscape protected as a World Heritage sand sea.
targetLabel: Namib Sand Sea — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: This desert teaches that aridity does not mean the complete absence of available moisture: fog is central to the ecology described by UNESCO. Sediment transport also links distant inland sources to a coastal dune system. The reference point is representative of the designated sand sea, not a unique centre of every dune.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
